editorial:
You follow a bored French teacher who gets pulled into a student’s strange essays about sneaking into a classmate’s home. The student is smart, quiet, and a little unsettling, while the teacher starts treating the essays like a gripping serial. The movie mixes dark humor, family drama, and mystery, so you never quite know what is real and what is made up. It feels like a smart thriller without being heavy, with sharp conversations and a creeping sense of trouble.

The acting is strong, especially the teacher and student, and the pacing keeps you curious even when scenes are just people talking. The downside is that the story can feel cold and morally messy, and some moments may make you uncomfortable. If you like character-driven mysteries and don’t need big action, this is a great pick. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Claude’s newest essay turns the camera on Germain himself, suggesting the student has been watching the teacher’s home and marriage too. Germain realizes he is no longer just the reader or mentor; he has become part of the story. The movie ends on an uneasy note, leaving you unsure how much of Claude’s writing was true and how much was invented, but making clear that his curiosity has crossed into dangerous territory.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves clever mysteries and character-driven thrillers.
